issues.description: The solution implementation is internally inconsistent about the Book struct's property name and its initializer labels. The problem statement specifies a Book with fields named title, author and genres (problem_statement.md lines 16-21). In the solution, the Book struct declares the title property as `bookTitle` (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 24-33) but the Client code constructs and accesses Books using the label/property name `title` (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift lines 34-41 and 10-12). This mismatch will prevent the code from compiling and will confuse students about the intended field name and initializer parameters.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Book struct's property names and initializer labels consistent with the problem statement and client usage. For example, rename `bookTitle` to `title` in solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so the synthesized memberwise initializer and property access match Client (Book(title: ..., author: ..., genres: ...); book.title). Alternatively, change the Client code to use `book.bookTitle` and construct Books with `Book(bookTitle: ..., author: ..., genres: ...)`. The preferred fix is to use `title` to align with the problem statement and the shown client usage.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies that a Book struct should have a property named `title` (and an optional `genres` array). In the provided solution implementation the Book struct defines the title property as `bookTitle` instead of `title`, while the solution's Client code (and the example usage) expects `book.title`. This naming divergence between the problem description and the solution implementation (and the mixed usage inside the solution itself) creates a direct mapping/confusion problem for students: they will expect to access `book.title` (per the exercise) but the authoritative Book implementation uses a different identifier `bookTitle`, and the solution's own client code is inconsistent with its Book definition.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the Book property name with the problem statement and client usage by renaming `bookTitle` to `title` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift (and update any references). Alternatively, change the client and example usages to reference `book.bookTitle` consistently and update the problem statement accordingly — preferred fix: rename to `title` so the implementation matches the exercise description and example outputs.
